changes.balance: The diplomatic channel cooled on the day the electoral constraint expired: Tehran restated its seven conditions, the strike moratorium lapsed, and a tanker was struck off Oman, while the flow accounting for October firmed up at 14.0 million barrels a day of crude and condensate through Hormuz, about 86 percent of pre-war and down from September's high on the combined measure. The inventory board is the open question: the API claims a fifth straight draw that neither survey saw, and the official print arbitrates it today.
changes.body: Brent Jan27 settled at $103.60 on Tuesday, down $1.17 or 1.12 percent, its lowest close since Oct 7, and WTI Dec26 settled at $96.09, down $0.37 or 0.38 percent (Reuters), after Iran's security council secretary posted that America's response to Iran's demands was not convincing and a senior Iranian official said the two sides remain far from a deal. Overnight Brent rose 76 cents to $104.36 and WTI rose 63 cents to $96.72 at 0730 GMT after Democrats captured both chambers of Congress. The API reported a crude draw of 5.267 million barrels for the week ending Oct 30, against a Wall Street Journal survey centred on a draw of 0.2 million and a Reuters poll centred on a build of 0.88 million; the official report is released today at 10:30 a.m. ET. December WCS is -$31.25 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 3) on 153 lots, a third wide traded front in four sessions, and December Houston traded at -$23.02 (ICE ARV settle, Nov 3) on 100 lots, putting the export spread at +$8.23. November Mainline apportionment (Light 19 percent, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert) is in effect. The validated diesel crack is $94.99 on the Nov 4 print.
changes.conditional: An official draw near the API figure confirms a tightening US balance into the winter; a print near the flat surveys grades the API as cargo timing. A published acceptance of the mediators' new suggestion would restart the reopening sequence; continued limited strikes inside the two month window before the new Congress sits keep the premium's escalation leg live.
changes.delta: Tuesday settles: Brent Jan27 $103.60, down $1.17 or 1.12 percent; WTI Dec26 $96.09, down $0.37 or 0.38 percent (Reuters). Overnight Brent $104.36, up 76 cents, and WTI $96.72, up 63 cents, at 0730 GMT after Democrats captured both chambers of Congress. API week ending Oct 30: crude -5.267 million barrels against a WSJ survey at -0.2 and a Reuters poll at +0.88. December WCS -$31.25 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 3) on 153 lots. December Houston -$23.02 (ICE ARV settle, Nov 3) on 100 lots, spread +$8.23. Diesel crack $94.99 on the validated history.
changes.source: Reuters, Nov 3-4, 2026; UKMTO incident 195-26, Nov 3, 2026; ICE Report Center EOD, Nov 3, 2026; API data via Reuters market sources, Nov 3, 2026; Wall Street Journal / Dow Jones survey, Nov 3, 2026; validated crack history refreshed Nov 4, 2026
changes.title: Brent fell a second day to its lowest close since Oct 7, the API printed a 5.267 million barrel draw against flat surveys, and December WCS widened again on traded volume

changes.balance: The quarter is a balance sheet statement: net debt down to C$1,751 million from C$7,147 million a year earlier, a higher dividend and stepped-up buybacks, on operating performance that held refining throughput through a turnaround by integration rather than by declaring the work done. The two open maintenance questions the release was expected to answer, Edmonton completion and the Base Plant fourth quarter item, remain open for the webcast.
changes.body: Suncor Energy released third quarter results on Nov 3 after the close: net earnings of C$3,814 million, adjusted operating earnings of C$4,631 million and record adjusted funds from operations of C$6,705 million. Upstream production averaged 852.5 kb/d, Oil Sands bitumen production was 948.0 kb/d with the year-on-year decrease attributed primarily to Syncrude mining maintenance and partly offset by record third quarter Firebag production, and net SCO production was 528.1 kb/d at 98 percent upgrader utilisation. Refinery throughput was 487.7 kb/d at 95 percent utilisation and refined product sales set a third quarter record at 676.9 kb/d. The release states that Suncor fully mitigated the expected throughput impacts of planned maintenance at its Edmonton refinery through regional integration; it is a mitigation statement, not a completion declaration, and the release carries no statement on Base Plant maintenance.
changes.conditional: A completion statement for Edmonton or a Base Plant fourth quarter statement on today's webcast closes those items; silence keeps them as guided items in the maintenance forecast.
changes.delta: Suncor Q3 (Nov 3): net earnings C$3,814 million, adjusted operating earnings C$4,631 million, record adjusted funds from operations C$6,705 million. Upstream 852.5 kb/d; bitumen 948.0 kb/d; SCO 528.1 kb/d at 98 percent upgrader utilisation; refining 487.7 kb/d at 95 percent; product sales a Q3 record at 676.9 kb/d; net debt C$1,751 million. Guidance unchanged; dividend up 10 percent to C$0.66; buybacks C$750 million a month from October.
changes.source: Suncor Energy third quarter 2026 results, Nov 3, 2026
changes.title: Suncor printed record funds from operations, and its release mitigates Edmonton maintenance without declaring it complete

changes.balance: The reserve programme is fully awarded and unchanged, so its remaining content is scheduling: deliveries out through December, and from early next year the return of more than 216 million barrels, 44 million of it premium barrels. The one open item is the heating oil reserve exchange, whose delivery deadline is Nov 13 with no award document posted.
changes.body: Checked directly on Nov 4, the Energy Department's newest reserve item remains the Oct 29 announcement completing the 172 million barrel commitment, and no new solicitation, award or changed award sheet has posted since the Nov 3 check. No award document has been posted for the Northeast heating oil reserve exchange; deliveries under it are due by Nov 13.
changes.conditional: A posted heating oil reserve award closes the last open reserve item. Any change to the posted award sheets, or a delivery schedule from the Department, updates the return timing.
changes.delta: No change since the Nov 3 direct check: newest reserve item remains the Oct 29 announcement; award sheets unchanged; heating oil reserve award still not posted (deliveries due Nov 13).
changes.source: US Department of Energy newsroom and SPR pages, checked directly Nov 4, 2026
changes.title: Reserves: a direct check on Nov 4 finds no new posting, and the heating oil award remains open

flags.body: Iran's security council secretary posted that America's response was not convincing and restated all seven conditions for reopening the strait; a senior Iranian official said the sides remain far from a deal; Qatari mediators expect feedback from both sides within 36 hours on a new bridging suggestion. The strike moratorium tied to Nov 3 has expired, and UKMTO incident 195-26 records a tanker struck by two projectiles in the engine room off Limah, Oman on Tuesday evening, with no casualties. An IRGC claim of four tankers hitting mines and two seizures is unconfirmed, with no vessel named. October flows on the fuller accounting: crude and condensate through Hormuz at 14.0 Mb/d, about 86 percent of pre-war, with combined exports down from September's high (Vortexa via Reuters, Nov 3).
flags.title: Hormuz: the channel cooled, the moratorium expired, a tanker was hit, and mediator feedback is due within 36 hours
flags.trigger: Feedback on the mediators' suggestion, a published agreement with accepted terms, a tier one flow print stepping in either direction, or a confirmed escalation beyond the limited-strike pattern

flags.body: November Mainline apportionment (Light 19 percent, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert) is in effect from Nov 1. December's outlook opens at persistence on those levels. The evidence pack for a December call now includes three traded December widenings in four sessions (-$31.10 on Oct 28, -$30.69 on Nov 2 and -$31.25 on Nov 3, the last on 153 lots) against one tightening print, plus a traded Houston spread at +$8.23. December nominations close Tuesday Nov 17; an unregistered call after that date is a lost data point for the prediction record.
flags.title: December apportionment: the nowcast is persistence at 19 and 7, no judgment call is registered, and nominations close Nov 17
flags.trigger: Registration of a December judgment call, the Enbridge December apportionment notice in mid November, or a material change in the November physical backdrop

flags.body: The API reported a crude draw of 5.267 million barrels for the week ending Oct 30, a fifth straight weekly decline on its count, against a Wall Street Journal survey centred on a draw of 0.2 million and a Reuters poll centred on a build of 0.88 million. The official report lands today at 10:30 a.m. ET, and its PADD 2 utilisation line, off 88.1 percent for the week ending Oct 23, tests the Midwest refinery recovery that the Canadian demand leg depends on.
flags.title: The API and the surveys disagree by five million barrels: today's inventory print arbitrates a wide gap
flags.trigger: The EIA release at 10:30 a.m. ET on Nov 4
